messages:
kai: quick thread 1: if we split admission -> coalescer with a minimal "cleanroom" boundary, are we just moving the serialization problem rather than solving it?
tess: not if the contract is a tokenized handoff. admission issues a lightweight ticket, coalescer claims it. no global locks.
ryan: main concern: memory churn and copying. pointer/ref handoff reduces copies but needs lifecycle management.
kai: right. two options: copy-handoff (safe, predictable) or pointer-handoff + lifecycle tokens (fast, GC-risk).
anya: for pointer-handoff we need either refcounts or epoch GC. also ensure observability: opaque batches hurt traces. emit minimal events: `batch.handoff {id, origin_ts, tenant}`.
tess: policy idea: default to copy-handoff for SLA tenants, pointer-handoff opt-in for best-effort. simplifies rollout and avoids p99 regressions for paying customers.
ryan: ran a small staging run: pointer-handoff lowered p50 by ~3ms but caused ~10-15% p99 regressions during GC spikes.
kai: tradeoff clear. Could we mitigate with a 3-way handshake: RESERVE -> FILL -> COMMIT? Adds a little protocol overhead but makes GC deterministic and gives clearer backpressure signals.
anya: handshake also makes telemetry simpler: each phase can emit a compact event, e.g., `batch.reserve`, `batch.commit`. stitchable in traces.
tess: another axis: handoff hysteresis. we saw ping-pong when we immediately re-enqueue micro-batches. simple time-window helps but causes priority inversion for SLA tenants.
kai: propose decay-hold: hold_ms = base * (1 - alpha * tenant_weight), tenant_weight 8..1). Bounded with min/max. add queue-depth bypass so system never stalls.
ryan: metric cardinality note: don't track per-tenant numeric weights in high-cardinality metrics. keep buckets: sla/standard/best-effort.
anya: tests: unit sim where many long best-effort requests flood and ensure SLA p99 stays within target. add e2e canary with feature-flag `cleanroom-handoff` + `pointer-handoff-opt-in`.
scheduler-bot: rollout plan queued: canary on 2 nodes -> observe p50/p95/p99 across tenant buckets -> rollout gating by p99 for SLA.
karesh: action items: kai protoype admission adapter for handshake + decay-hold, tess will run canary tuning, ryan to produce perf microbench results, anya to draft RFC addendum (handoff tokens, tracing events, per-tenant defaults).
tess: one more ops thing: emit `batch.handoff.hold_ms` and `batch.handoff.kind` (copy|pointer|handshake) as low-cardinality tags.
kai: PR by EOW, canary next week. thanks all. :thumbsup:
